Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

oasr 0.1.0.9000 (development)

Breaking changes

  • sample_abs_data is now a genuine loan-level dataset: twelve fixed-rate mortgages with original_balance, balance, wac, servicing, io_strip, accrual_method, term, age, ltv, fico and three descriptive columns. Each balance is derived by amortising original_balance over age months, so the four fields are mutually consistent. The previous version carried wam and market_price but no term, which meant project_cashflows() and calculate_oas() could not run on it at all; the README and vignette examples both failed. Code that reconstructed the term as wam + age should now read term directly.
  • sample_deal_structure is re-tranched onto the new pool. Its three bonds sum to the pool’s current balance, as before.
  • summary.oas_result() returns convergence$converged as a logical rather than the string "Yes"/"No". print() still prints Yes/No.

Conventions

These change results by default. Each is a modelling convention that oasr previously fixed with no way to vary it; the earlier behaviour remains reachable, and setting every option below to its legacy value reproduces the previous release bit for bit.

  • accrual_method is read per loan, from an accrual_method column, then from an Accrual column (the spelling the surrounding suite already carries), then from the new argument of the same name on project_cashflows(), project_cashflows_with_io() and calculate_oas(). "30/360" is the default and is computed exactly as before, never from a calendar: for a monthly-pay amortising loan it is one twelfth by construction. "ACT/365" and "ACT/360" accrue on actual days and need a date anchor, supplied as start_date or a per-loan accrual_start_date; without one the engine warns once and falls back to 30/360. ACT/365 redistributes the same annual interest across months, while ACT/360 raises the annual total by 365/360.
  • terminal_balance defaults to "return": the balance outstanding when the projection stops is paid as a final cash flow. Dropping it priced a 300-month pool against a 24-month horizon at a fraction of its worth, with nothing to say so. "drop" restores the old behaviour.
  • on_short_horizon defaults to "warn" when n_periods is shorter than the longest remaining term. "silent" and "error" are also accepted.
  • recovery_basis defaults to "defaults": recovery is taken on the amount that actually defaulted recovery_lag months earlier. The old "balance" basis took it on the whole balance standing at the time, which delivered about 0.55 of defaults where the model asked for 0.65.
  • discounting on calculate_present_value(), calculate_duration_convexity() and calculate_oas() defaults to "path", compounding the shortest simulated rate along each path. That is the Monte Carlo definition of an option-adjusted spread. "spot" is the earlier behaviour, where each cash flow was discounted at the reference yield standing in its own period, taken as a zero rate to that maturity.
  • calculate_duration_convexity() gains reproject. Given a function that projects cash flows under a shocked curve, it computes a true effective duration with prepayments responding to the shock. It stays opt-in because re-projecting roughly triples the cost, not because the default is better.
  • calculate_oas() records the conventions it ran under in result$options, and run_oas_sensitivity() and create_oas_surface() re-solve on them. A sensitivity built from a spot-discounted result no longer silently reverts to the defaults.
  • simulate_rates() names the columns of its yield matrices by period, so the leading t = 0 column is visible rather than implied, and gains include_t0. It defaults to TRUE, keeping that column: path discounting needs it, because the rate prevailing over month 1 is the one observed at time 0. FALSE returns exactly n_periods columns.
  • The three plotting functions take a seed, so a sampled plot reproduces.

New

  • cashflow_components() returns the component position of each cash flow array by name, for the asset, asset-with-IO and bond layouts. The positions themselves are unchanged; they are now written down in one place instead of appearing as bare numbers across four files and the test suite.

Bug fixes

  • The structured branch of calculate_oas() applied the bond weights and then divided by total bond balance a second time. On sample_deal_structure that put the price near 60 when it belonged near 103, so the structured path could not converge on any price near par. It now solves: 98 bps against a target of

  • calculate_present_value() and calculate_average_life() consider every non-zero flow rather than only the positive ones. A negative total is a real outflow, and dropping it overstated the present value. For cash flows this package generates the two agree, since those totals are non-negative; the difference shows up on user-supplied cash flows carrying a writedown.

  • aggregate_cashflows() and plot_prepayment_rates() no longer fail on one-asset pools, where the [t, , ] slice collapsed to a vector.

  • create_oas_report() works. Two separate faults had to clear before it could: the data file path was recovered from the generated chunk text by a greedy regex that left a trailing quote on the filename, and the parameter table was built with sapply(), which returns a list when seasonal_factors is twelve long and every other element is one, after which data.frame() expanded that list into columns and demanded twelve rows against nine names. The second only shows once the first is fixed and pandoc is present, so it had never been reached.

  • create_oas_report() can find its own data file. The path was recovered from the generated chunk text by a greedy regex that left a trailing quote on the filename, so rendering always failed.

  • get_discount_factors() and binary_search_oas() clamp period lookups into range. A time under half a month rounded to index 0.

  • calculate_oas() passes reference_rates down to project_cashflows(), so pools containing variable rate loans are reachable through it. A new reference_key argument selects the index; it defaults to the 10-year.

  • calculate_oas() derives converged from whether the price tolerance was met rather than from the iteration count. A solve that converged on its last allowed iteration previously reported failure and emitted a warning.

  • plot_cashflows() maps total to component 9. It previously mapped it to 8, which holds servicing.

  • project_cashflows() and project_cashflows_with_io() check their required columns up front and name the missing ones.

  • plot_yield_surface() no longer relies on an unimported %>%.

Performance and structure

  • calculate_oas() computes the credit vectors, the cash flow projection and the weighted average life once, before the bisection loop, rather than on every trial spread; none of the three takes the OAS as an input. Duration and convexity likewise move after the search, since they are wanted for the answer rather than for the solve. Only the present value stays in the loop. A nine-iteration solve runs roughly four to seven times faster depending on load, and every returned value is bit-identical to before.
  • project_cashflows() and project_cashflows_with_io() share one engine. They differed only by the IO strip, and the loop, the validation and the parallel plumbing had been copied between them; the file is about 210 lines shorter and the socket-cluster branch now exists once.
  • calculate_present_value() and calculate_average_life() read the columns they need directly instead of materialising a whole period-by-component matrix per asset first. Present value is about twice as fast; the values are unchanged.
  • Removed a second, verbatim copy of the internal .compute_asset_vectors(), which shadowed an identical definition 136 lines above it, and folded the two identical copies of the prepayment-model scaler in run_oas_sensitivity() and create_oas_surface() into one internal helper.
  • Conditional prepayment rates are capped just below 1. A sensitivity multiplier of 2 on a fast base speed previously made the annual-to-monthly conversion undefined and produced NaN.

Documentation and packaging

  • The vignette and README no longer attach dnsr. It exports plot_yield_curves() and plot_yield_surface() of its own, so attaching it after oasr masked both, and a vignette chunk calling oasr’s signature against dnsr’s function failed with unused arguments. Every dnsr call in either document was already dnsr:: qualified, so nothing needed it attached. The collision is documented in the README, and a test fails if a third shared name ever appears.

  • oasr-package.R moved into R/, where roxygen reads it. Its import directives had never been applied.

  • rmarkdown is no longer imported into the namespace while sitting in Suggests, which made R CMD check fail at the dependency gate. plotly and lattice are declared in Suggests.

  • LICENSE holds the two-field stub R expects; the full MIT text is in LICENSE.md. VignetteBuilder: knitr is declared, and the vignette runs.

  • calculate_duration_convexity() documents its sign convention: it returns the signed logarithmic derivative (1/P) dP/dy, not the negated fixed-income reading.

  • The R-CMD-check and parallel-paths workflows run on push and pull request again. Both had been manual-only: dnsr was private, the default token is scoped to this repository alone, and so an automatic run failed at the dependency gate before reaching a single check. dnsr is public now and the default token resolves it, so neither workflow carries the personal-token fallback any longer. The README drops the GITHUB_PAT step it asked of readers for the same reason.

  • The package has a pkgdown site, at https://ambientpointcorp.github.io/oasr. There was no _pkgdown.yml and no workflow to render one, so the reference index fell back to whatever order pkgdown guessed and the vignette was reachable only by building it locally. The index now groups the 36 exported topics by what they do, and URL: and BugReports: are declared in DESCRIPTION, which had neither.
